blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Automation means using software to do repetitive tasks without a human every time. For example, sending confirmation emails, generating invoices, or checking numbers against a rule.

Digital transformation is a bigger idea. It means changing the way a company works by putting digital tools at the centre of how it operates. Automation is a tool inside transformation — it is not the same thing. Many companies have automated small steps without really transforming anything. Others have transformed their whole operation by rethinking every process, piece by piece.

Over the last few years, most companies have quietly become more digital than they realised. The question now is simple: is it happening to them, or with them?

items.q: What does automation do?
options: It writes new rules for the market
It does repetitive tasks without a human every time
items.why: "Automation means using software to do repetitive tasks without a human every time."

items.q: According to the text, is automation the same as digital transformation?
options: No, transformation is only about people
Yes, but only in big companies
Yes, they are exactly the same
No, automation is a tool inside transformation
items.why: "Automation is a tool inside transformation — it is not the same thing."

items.q: How did some companies transform their whole operation?
options: By rethinking every process, piece by piece
items.why: "Others have transformed their whole operation by rethinking every process, piece by piece."

items.q: The text says most companies "quietly became more digital than they realised." This suggests that…
options: the change happened slowly, without much notice
digital tools are always a mistake
the change was loud and planned
no company has changed at all
items.why: Inferência: "quietly" e "than they realised" mostram uma mudança lenta e pouco percebida.

items.q: The author would most likely AGREE that…
options: digital tools are not useful for any company
automating small steps already means real transformation
real transformation needs rethinking how the company works
a company should just buy tools and stop thinking
items.why: Inferência: o texto separa "automar pequenos passos" de "transformar repensando os processos".

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie ajudando um novo gestor. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi, thanks for the coffee. So, you said your team automated the invoices last month? That is great. But let me ask you one question first.

When you automated them, did you change how the invoices work? Or did the software just do the same old steps faster? Because those are two very different things.

Here is what I mean. Last year, my team automated our confirmation emails. The emails went out in one second, not one hour. Everyone was happy. But the process behind them was still messy. We just made a slow, messy job faster. That is automation, but it is not transformation.

Real transformation is when you stop and ask, "Why do we do it this way at all?" You rethink the whole process, piece by piece. Sometimes you find you do not even need that step.

So my advice is simple. Do not stop at "we automated the invoices." Look at the process first. Ask what the invoice is really for. Then decide what to automate. Start small, but start with the process, not the tool.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What did the new manager's team do last month?
items.why: "you said your team automated the invoices last month?"

items.q: What happened when Sophie's team automated the confirmation emails?
options: The emails went out much faster, but the process was still messy
The team deleted all the emails
items.why: "The emails went out in one second... But the process behind them was still messy."

items.q: What is Sophie's advice to the manager?
options: Look at the process first, then decide what to automate
Buy the most expensive tool first
items.why: "Look at the process first... start with the process, not the tool."

items.q: Sophie says "we just made a slow, messy job faster." This suggests that…
options: the team should work more slowly
speed alone does not fix a bad process
automation is always a bad idea
items.why: Inferência: um trabalho ruim feito rápido continua ruim — velocidade não resolve o processo.

items.q: How would you best describe Sophie's tone?
items.why: Inferência: ela elogia ("That is great"), mas dá um conselho sincero e claro.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We use automation to send invoices at night." Automation means…
options: software doing a task without a human every time
a meeting with the whole team
items.why: Automation = automação: o software faz a tarefa sozinho.

items.q: "Sending the same email every day is a repetitive task." A repetitive task is…
options: a job you do again and again
a job you do only once
items.why: Repetitive task = tarefa repetitiva, feita muitas vezes.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The system can ___ an invoice for every order automatically."
items.why: To generate = gerar; o sistema gera a fatura.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Before we buy any tool, we need to ___ how our invoices really work."
items.why: To rethink = repensar; olhar o processo de novo antes de mudar.

items.q: "After the meeting, I began to realise we were already very digital." To realise means to…
options: start to understand or notice something
items.why: To realise = perceber, dar-se conta de algo.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre automação e mudança. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "We will roll out the new system next month." To roll out means to…
options: start using it, step by step
items.why: Roll out = colocar em uso, geralmente aos poucos.

items.q: "The manager still has to sign off on the new process." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "Some people pushed back on the new tool." This means they…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar.

items.q: "We agreed on the plan, but nobody followed through." This means they…
options: did not finish what they planned
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Let's start small and automate one task first." To start small means to…
options: begin with something simple, not everything at once
items.why: Start small = começar por algo pequeno e simples antes de crescer.
